I'm seeing the issue now — when the USB device disconnects, `typec_deattach` gets called before `device_del`, which means the typec link removal tries to access a kernfs directory that's already been deleted. The sysfs_remove_link fails because the parent kobj has a null sd pointer, triggering the warning about the missing directory.

The stale pointer problem happens when `port->usb2_dev` still points to a USB device whose sysfs directory was already removed — this occurs if `typec_deattach` never gets called (maybe the connector was unbound first or was NULL at disconnect time). Later when `ucsi_unregister_partner` tries to unlink that device, it hits the same kernfs warning because the kobj.sd is already gone.

I need to check the exact line numbers in the 7.0 tree where this warning fires and look for any upstream fixes that handle the `typec_partner_unlink_device` or `usb2_dev` cleanup.

The line number discrepancy in the warning is expected since it's referencing an older version of the file. Now I'll write up the report.
## Root cause analysis

### 1. The warning itself — `parent == NULL`, not "entry missing"

`fs/kernfs/dir.c:1724-1734` (in the OEM 6.17 tree this WARN is at line 1706):

```c
int kernfs_remove_by_name_ns(struct kernfs_node *parent, const char *name,
			     const struct ns_common *ns)
{
	if (!parent) {
		WARN(1, KERN_WARNING "kernfs: can not remove '%s', no directory\n", name);
		return -ENOENT;
	}
```

So `-ENOENT`/"no directory" is emitted **only** when the caller passed a NULL `kernfs_node` parent, i.e. `kobj->sd == NULL` in `sysfs_remove_link()` (`fs/sysfs/symlink.c:143-153`) — the kobject's sysfs directory is already gone/never existed. The name being removed is `"typec"`, which pins the caller exactly.

### 2. Who removes `"typec"`

Only one place in the tree creates/removes a link named `typec`:

- `drivers/usb/typec/class.c:892` — `sysfs_create_link(&dev->kobj, &partner->dev.kobj, "typec")` in `typec_partner_link_device()` (`class.c:888`)
- `drivers/usb/typec/class.c:909` — `sysfs_remove_link(&dev->kobj, "typec")` in `typec_partner_unlink_device()` (`class.c:906`)

Here `dev` is the **enumerated `struct usb_device`** stored in `port->usb2_dev` / `port->usb3_dev`.

### 3. The offending chain

`drivers/usb/typec/ucsi/ucsi.c:1264` `ucsi_handle_connector_change()` (workqueue `events`, matching `Comm: kworker/6:0`) → on connect-change with `!CONNECTED`, `ucsi.c:1325` calls `ucsi_unregister_partner()` (`ucsi.c:1138`) → `ucsi.c:1151` `typec_unregister_partner(con->partner)` → `class.c:1174`:

```c
	mutex_lock(&port->partner_link_lock);
	if (port->usb2_dev) {                                  /* class.c:1184 */
		typec_partner_unlink_device(partner, port->usb2_dev);  /* class.c:1185 */
		port->usb2_dev = NULL;
	}
```

`port->usb2_dev` is **stale** here: it still points at a `usb_device` that has already been disconnected and whose kobject/sysfs dir is torn down (`kobj->sd == NULL`), hence `sysfs_remove_link(&dev->kobj, "typec")` → `kernfs_remove_by_name(NULL, "typec")` → WARN + `-ENOENT`. `dev_name(dev)` at `class.c:908` on the same freed device is the potential use-after-free variant.

### 4. Why the pointer goes stale — the asymmetry in usb core

`drivers/usb/core/port.c:695` `connector_bind()` sets `port_dev->connector` and, at `port.c:716-717`, calls `typec_attach()` if a child device is already present (which sets `port->usb2_dev`/`usb3_dev` via `typec_partner_attach()`, `class.c:2144`).

Its mirror, `connector_unbind()` at **`drivers/usb/core/port.c:722-728` in this tree**, does *not* call `typec_deattach()`:

```c
	sysfs_remove_link(&connector->kobj, dev_name(dev));
	sysfs_remove_link(&dev->kobj, "connector");
	port_dev->connector = NULL;            /* port.c:728 */
```

On dock unplug the component framework unbinds first, clearing `port_dev->connector`. `usb_disconnect()` then does `typec_deattach(port_dev->connector, &udev->dev)` at `drivers/usb/core/hub.c:2363` — a **no-op** because `connector` is already NULL — so `typec_partner_deattach()` (`class.c:2168`, which would clear `port->usb2_dev/usb3_dev` at `class.c:2178-2181`) never runs. The device is then freed (`hub.c:2376 device_del`, `hub.c:2393 hub_free_dev`), leaving the dangling pointer that UCSI's later connector-change work dereferences.

Note the existing partial hardening does *not* cover this: `ec27386de23a` ("usb: typec: class: Fix NULL pointer access") added `partner_link_lock`, and `66e1a887273c` ("Invalidate USB device pointers on partner unregistration") added the `= NULL` at `class.c:1186/1190` — both only serialize/clean up *after* the bad pointer has already been used.

### 5. Upstream fix — exists upstream, NOT in this tree

Commit **`e0b291fe117964037e0ba382eff4bb365d531c3a`** — "usb: core: port: Deattach Type-C connector on component unbind", Chia-Lin Kao (AceLan) <acelan.kao@canonical.com>, `Fixes: 11110783f5ea ("usb: Inform the USB Type-C class about enumerated devices")`, `Cc: stable`, merged by Greg KH via `https://patch.msgid.link/20260611071201.1235545-1-acelan.kao@canonical.com`. Its commit message quotes verbatim the same splat (`kernfs: can not remove 'typec', no directory`, `CPU: 6 PID: 55`, `Workqueue: events ucsi_handle_connector_change`), and mentions the Thunderbolt-dock igc/AER fallout.

Fix:

```c
 	sysfs_remove_link(&dev->kobj, "connector");
+	if (port_dev->child)
+		typec_deattach(port_dev->connector, &port_dev->child->dev);
 	port_dev->connector = NULL;
```

Presence in this tree:
- `git describe --contains e0b291fe1179` → **`v7.2-rc5~7^2~10`**
- `git merge-base --is-ancestor e0b291fe1179 HEAD` → **NOT IN HEAD** (this checkout is `v7.0`, `028ef9c96e96`)
- Confirmed by inspection: `drivers/usb/core/port.c:722-728` still lacks the `typec_deattach()` call.

### Verdict

Root cause is the missing `typec_deattach()` in `connector_unbind()` (`drivers/usb/core/port.c:722`), leaving stale `port->usb2_dev`/`usb3_dev` that `typec_unregister_partner()` (`drivers/usb/typec/class.c:1184-1191`) feeds to `typec_partner_unlink_device()` (`class.c:906-909`), whose `sysfs_remove_link(&dev->kobj, "typec")` hits `kernfs_remove_by_name_ns()`'s `!parent` WARN (`fs/kernfs/dir.c:1730`). The fix is upstream as `e0b291fe1179` (v7.2-rc5, stable-tagged) and must be backported to the 6.17-oem kernel; it is absent from this v7.0 tree.
